research.website_note: The homepage and company pages on transistor.fm identify the website as Transistor's podcast hosting platform.

strategy.observation: Transistor already hosts branded podcasts, including shows from Kit.com.
strategy.offer_link: A referral partnership could give Transistor’s B2B customers access to audio editing and show notes alongside their hosting, while giving the Partnerships Lead a complementary service to evaluate rather than another hosting product.
hypotheses: Some of Transistor’s B2B customers may want outside help editing episodes and preparing show notes.
The Partnerships Lead may be open to referring customers to production providers.
Transistor may not already have a preferred partner covering these services.
strategy.angle: With Kit.com’s branded shows already on Transistor, would an audio-editing and show-notes partner be useful for other B2B customers?
strategy.fit_reason: The offer complements podcast hosting and is relevant to Transistor’s demonstrated branded-show customer base. The plausible route is a customer referral partnership, not an assumed need for Transistor to buy production services itself.

draft.subject: Production support for B2B podcast customers
draft.body:
Hi there,

Seeing Kit.com among your podcast customers made me wonder whether other B2B teams might want outside help with the work between recording and publishing.

I provide podcast audio editing and show notes for B2B brands. If customers ask for that kind of support, a referral partnership could give them a production option alongside their hosting, without adding that work to your team.

Could I send a sample edit and show notes for you to assess as a potential referral option?
